naming.files: one file per attempted law at <lean dir>/<law id>.lean (lean dirs gen/M1/lean, gen/M2/lean, gen/M2/extracted/m1/lean, gen/M3/lean), one model file per Bend model at <lean dir>/models/<model stem>.lean, one report.json per lean dir; nothing else in those directories
naming.fixed: St, Act, Obs, Reach, Cell, Bytes, step, run, s0, obs
naming.identifiers: every name taken from a facts or linked document gets a fixed prefix, so no generated identifier is a Lean keyword or a word of tests_m3/_i43.py::LEAN_BANNED (whole words only): record type T -> T_T, its field x -> f_x; state field x -> St.f_x; action a -> constructor Act.a_a with input binders i_<input>; observer o -> ob_o; migration m -> mig_m; model function f (last_ok, runs_ok, no_code, perm, cost, elapsed, is_<a>, consumers) -> fn_f; site and hit predicates of a SORT site -> site_<x> and hit_<x> (x: the law id after L_sort_site_, holon.sorts.sites rule R7), the site's raw obligation -> ro_<x>; linked record carrier C -> R_C, its byte k of field F -> f_<F with . written __>_<k>; linked function f -> c_f, a loader's condition -> c_ok_<loader>; a view erasing fields F1..Fn -> V_<F sorted, joined by __> with its projection view_<..>; statement binders -> v_<IR name>; oracle parameters in Reach -> p_<name>. Never an escaped identifier (guillemets).
naming.namespace: every model definition lives in `namespace Model` (one `namespace Model` ... `end Model` block per file); every frozen statement refers to it as Model.<name>; no other namespace, no `open`
naming.theorems: at top level, after the marker line `-- holon:theorems`: a PROVED law's theorem is named exactly its law id; a REFUTED law's counter-law is <law id>_counter and its refutation <law id>_refuted (I9)

readings.linked: Lean cells are Option (BitVec 8): a record's byte is a BitVec 8 where Bend's is a U32, so Lean's theorems cover byte-valued records only (a narrower domain than Bend's, I9 Surprise 5); an undefined cell (Bend 57005) is none, and the decoders' orderings compare it as 57005; every premise is a hypothesis where Bend pins a field to a constant or to another record's field (an equivalent statement)
readings.machine: Lean reads the holon-facts/0.2 document itself (holon.gen.lean_machine), the target library through its Lean twin (hand-written target input, like the Bend library: common mode, I9 Question 4); Nat, Bool and lists as in Bend; premises are hypotheses as in Bend; the statement is the frozen Lean text of the same IR
readings.machine_oracle: as machine, and: the Fn<List<Nat>,Nat> oracle parameter is a Lean function (List Nat -> Nat) where Bend ranges over finite tables (first matching entry, else 0), each of which is such a function, so the Lean theorem implies the Bend one; Reach is the same inductive set; the site predicate is Lean's own reading of rules R8-R10 (holon.gen.lean_sites) over the site's raw obligation ro_<x>; on every PROVED site the site predicate is constantly true (coercion_guard never uses Reach), so rule L7 pins where a site is hit (hit_<x>) and the raw obligation (ro_<x>), each taking both values on the samples, and rule L4 requires site_<x> to reach ro_<x>
